title: What Makes Hard Water Hard?
description: Chemistry Hard-Water Analysis: a manual-faithful practice sequence followed by teacher-approved gravimetric analysis of two preconcentrated water samples, six-sample class ranking, and a qualified client recommendation. All balance outputs and peer results in this standalone simulator are explicitly teacher-configured simulated evidence.
learningGoals: Use limiting-reactant and Ksp reasoning to design complete Ca2+ precipitation as CaCO3.
Collect separate observations, simulated measurements, tare-corrected calculations, and uncertainty evidence through gravimetric analysis.
Correct a 20 mL preconcentrated aliquot result by the stated 200x factor and report original-source hardness in mg/L as CaCO3.
Pool six class results, defend the method, and write a qualified client recommendation.
safetyNotes: Wear splash-proof goggles; solutions may be harmful if swallowed and may irritate eyes.
Use only the teacher-approved vacuum-filtration configuration and confirm the receiver before pouring.
Use heat-safe handling at 110-120 C and never weigh a warm watch-glass assembly.
Follow the configured disposal path: approved liquids to the drain, paper and precipitate to solid waste, and rubbing alcohol for marker cleanup.
